subject: Request: Contract SLA term modification & commercial exception for Helion Health
messages:
From: Carmen Lopez <carmen.lopez@helionhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO ask: uptime floor + credit cap for pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profile on the m-8 instances. Before we can spin up a 3-month pilot, procurement needs two items in our contract:

1) An uptime floor of 99.6% for the pilot region (us-west) with a defined remediation ladder.
2) A cap on cumulative service credits at 5% of monthly committed spend. We can accept a graduated credit schedule but not an open-ended remedy.

Also, given the pilot budget, we need a 20% first-year commercial discount tied to committed vCPU-hours.

Can Redwood contractually accept these deviations from standard SLA language? If not, what can you offer as an alternative mitigation?

Best,
Carmen
VP, Platform Engineering
Helion Health

Subject: Re: SLO ask: uptime floor + credit cap for pilot

Hi Carmen — appreciate the clarity.

Short answer: we can likely accommodate a narrower uptime floor and a credit cap, but both require deal-desk and finance sign-off because they affect remedy exposure and unit economics. I’ve looped Jordan (pricing) and will run a short internal review.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll draft a compact SLO amendment that defines the 99.6% floor for the pilot region, a 3-step remediation ladder (automated retries + temporary burst capacity + prorated credit), and a 5% cumulative credit cap.
- Jordan to confirm the commercial impact and whether we can pair that with a time-bound 20% pilot discount.
- If needed, we’ll route to Marissa for executive approval on commercial exceptions.

Target: come back with a proposed amendment and commercial summary by Friday EOD. Would that work for your procurement timeline?

Cheers,
Mateo
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SLO ask: commercial impact and options

Team — quick read: Helion's ask (99.6% uptime + 5% credit cap + 20% discount) is doable but reduces expected margin materially for the pilot. Financials: with the proposed credit cap we limit worst-case exposure which is positive, but the 20% discount on committed capacity knocks ~18% off gross contribution for the pilot months.

Options:
A) Approve as-is for a fixed 3-month pilot, with the discount applied only to consumed committed hours and a maximum credit cap of 5% (recommended).
B) Approve uptime floor but reduce discount to 12% and add a consumption threshold (first 500k tokens at full price, remainder discounted).
C) Push for a shorter credit window (single-month cumulative cap) instead of pilot-wide cap to reduce tail risk.

If we go with A, this needs Marissa's executive OK because it's outside standard deal desk parameters (discount >15% + SLA carveout).

I’ll attach a quick P&L and the delta by option.

-Jordan
Head of Pricing & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: helion_pilot_pnl.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO ask: commercial impact and options

Thanks Jordan — read the delta. My view: we can greenlight option A strictly for a 3-month pilot with three caveats:

1) The 20% discount is limited to the pilot term only and automatically reverts to standard rates unless a renewal is signed.
2) The 5% credit cap applies to the pilot months in aggregate but must be accompanied by a remediation playbook (operations steps + escalation ladder) that Helion agrees to in writing.
3) Legal to add a clause that excludes credits for outages caused by customer misconfiguration or scheduled maintenance aligned with our published windows.

Approve on the condition that Procurement signs the playbook and the finance owner confirms the accounting treatment for pilot credits. Jordan/Kim, coordinate with Legal and Finance and return the final redline; I’ll sign off after review.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
